body.summary: Four humans die and wake in a brightly coloured afterlife neighbourhood run by an architect called Michael, who tells them they are in the Good Place. Eleanor Shellstrop, a selfish Arizona saleswoman, realises she was mistaken for a do-gooder of the same name and recruits her assigned soulmate, ethics professor Chidi, to teach her to be good. ||The neighbourhood is revealed to be a torture experiment designed by Michael and his demon staff; the four humans escape to the afterlife's bureaucracy, petition the Judge, are returned to Earth alive to prove they can improve, and eventually build a new system that lets souls earn their way into the Good Place. The finale has each of them choose, in time, to walk through a door and dissolve into the universe.||

arcs.summary: Eleanor hides her mistaken identity and takes ethics lessons from Chidi while the neighbourhood's oddities pile up.
The neighbourhood is exposed as a Bad Place experiment; Michael is repeatedly rebooted and the humans try to escape.
The four petition the Judge, are sent back to Earth alive, and try to become better people in a new timeline.
Michael and the humans design a new afterlife system where souls can improve over many lifetimes.
The group reaches the real Good Place, finds it stagnant, and each eventually chooses to leave through the door.

notable_scenes.summary: Eleanor realises she does not belong and confesses to Chidi, who agrees to teach her ethics in secret.
Michael reveals the neighbourhood is the Bad Place and the humans have been torturing each other.
Michael explains the Jeremy Bearimy timeline on a whiteboard.
The Judge rules on the humans and sends them back to Earth.
The group tours the real Good Place and finds its residents numb and bored.
Eleanor walks through the door and dissolves into the universe.
